# Skillbench 0.2.0

Skillbench 0.2 makes the local workflow repeatable: initialize once, run commands with
their defaults, and open a readable result bundle after every interactive run.

## Changelog

### One project layout

- Project configuration now lives at `.skillbench/config.yaml`.
- Development evals and editable runtime assets also live under `.skillbench/`.
- Only generated state such as runs, caches, temporary workspaces, history, and Web
  storage is ignored by Git.
- `inspect` can initialize an interactive project once; later commands discover and
  reuse that project from subdirectories.

### Automatic, collision-free run output

- Interactive `inspect`, `eval`, `compare`, and `merge` commands automatically save a
  unique bundle under `.skillbench/runs/<command>/` by default.
- Repeating a command no longer collides with an existing default destination.
- Use `--no-output` for a transient interactive run, or `--output <directory>` for an
  exact destination. Automation remains explicit and writes only when `--output` is
  supplied.

### Less repetitive runner setup

- Interactive commands offer one compact confirmation to reuse the configured runner,
  model, reasoning effort, and sandbox.
- Declining opens the detailed selector without changing the project configuration.
- CLI overrides and non-interactive execution remain deterministic.

### Clearer evaluations and reports

- Eval prompts, starter content, preflight summaries, and errors now explain the YAML
  tasks and assertions being loaded.
- Every saved bundle has a root `report.md` and a stable directory structure.
- Merge bundles contain every candidate, a development winner in `recommended/`, and a
  `final/` skill only after successful holdout validation.
- Merge reports explain incompatible scopes in plain language and suggest concrete next
  actions.
- The Web application validates every manifest-referenced result, source, report,
  artifact, and instruction before persistence.

## Migrate from 0.1 to 0.2

There is intentionally no automatic migration. From the root of an existing 0.1
project, move the versioned project files into the new layout:

```sh
mkdir -p .skillbench
mv skillbench.yaml .skillbench/config.yaml
mv evals .skillbench/evals
mv skillbench/assets.yaml skillbench/judge skillbench/prompts skillbench/templates .skillbench/
rmdir skillbench
```

Persist the new default run directory if the configuration does not already contain an
`outputs` section:

```sh
if ! grep -q '^outputs:' .skillbench/config.yaml; then
  printf '\noutputs:\n  directory: .skillbench/runs\n' >> .skillbench/config.yaml
fi
```

The 0.1 initializer ignored the whole `.skillbench/` directory. Replace that rule with
targeted generated-state rules so configuration, evals, and runtime assets can be
committed:

```sh
sed -i.bak '\|^\.skillbench/$|d' .gitignore
rm .gitignore.bak
cat >> .gitignore <<'EOF'
.skillbench/runs/
.skillbench/tmp/
.skillbench/promptfoo/
.skillbench/cli-history.json
.skillbench/web/
.skillbench/skillbench-web.sqlite
EOF
```

Finally, verify the migrated project and review the files before committing them:

```sh
npx @thisisjuke/skillbench@0.2.0 doctor
git status --short
```

Existing generated caches and Web data already inside `.skillbench/` are preserved.
Old root-level `skillbench.yaml`, `evals/`, and `skillbench/` paths are no longer used
for automatic project discovery.
